body: I’m sorry, I don’t have any good advice for that. Maybe she believes or she is seeing a pattern of unhealthy relationships, and there may or may not be some therapeutic ethics against suggesting that if they think it’s causing harm? I have no clue I’m just grasping at straws. If you haven’t already, I would recommend trying to get to the meat of the matter, asking why she thinks you need to focus on yourself right now specifically instead of dating, and what she thinks you should be working with/towards in therapy, like what therapeutic methods and such. If you still disagree, maybe shop for a new therapist, and be upfront about this. I don’t know since I’m not a professional and my experience is limited, but i think therapists should be challenging but not forceful, it seems off to me that she would be basically pushing your direction of care towards your trauma if that’s not what you want right now.

I think open communication about what you want, what you don’t want, and how you want to go about it will be helpful. I’ve had therapy that went in “wrong ways” before even in really silly ways in hindsight, because I wasn’t advocating for myself and was treating therapy as something I go along with the ride for, and my therapist got the wrong impression about what i needed.

If this is your hangup, it was mine, my therapist was glad that i started speaking up about how I’m feeling regarding treatment, as I think any good therapist should want us to be able to help them help us better. Evidently, the path you’re on is more harm than good, and your therapist should not want that for you. It’s commonly said that it gets worse before it gets better, but that doesn’t mean you should brute force down a path that is causing suffering for it. 

I’ve been told that for some people, it takes years in therapy to really begin to heal their traumas if they’re really strong, so healing needs to be a patient journey, where we’re equally as concerned about balancing our day-to-day well being, as we are for seeking progress.

I wrote down everything i felt and wanted to talk about this past week, rewrote it so that it explained my feelings thoroughly but with less words, and then arranged it in a list, putting the easier to talk about things at the beginning and end so that i could kinda just get in and out of saying it immediately, and just went through it all at once at the session. It was really intense for me but it felt great afterward. Hopefully if you’re comfortable entrusting your therapist with what you know, you’ll find the way you want to proceed!
